description:
Housing Support Coordinator

Location: Based across Bradford and Keighley

Hours: 37 hours on a rota basis, which factors in one week (Monday-Friday) of lates every 5 weeks. Late shifts are 2pm-10pm. And also, one Saturday and one Sunday every 5 weeks. This includes bank holidays.

Working in partnership, Waythrough and The Bridge Project deliver the Bradford Temporary Accommodation Service on behalf of Bradford Metropolitan District Council, providing safe, supportive, and temporary accommodation for women who present as homeless to the Local Authority.

As a Housing Support Coordinator, you will play a key role in empowering women to achieve greater stability, independence, and positive outcomes. The service supports women who have experienced homelessness and may also have a history of offending, vulnerabilities, complex support needs, or be at risk of involvement with the criminal justice system.

Based across Bradford and Keighley, you will work alongside individuals living in temporary accommodation, providing person-centred support tailored to their unique circumstances. Your role will involve helping women to address housing issues, overcome barriers to independence, and access the services and opportunities they need to rebuild their lives.

This is a rewarding opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of women who have experienced homelessness and significant adversity. The role requires a flexible, compassionate, and trauma-informed approach, balancing housing management responsibilities with high-quality support delivery.

Successful candidates will be committed to working collaboratively with partners, advocating for the needs of service users, and helping individuals move towards greater independence, stability, and social inclusion. Through building positive relationships and providing practical, person-centred support, you will contribute to creating lasting change for some of the most vulnerable women within our communities.

Please note that this position is delivered on a rolling rota framework and requires the successful candidate to work a range of shift patterns, including early shifts, to ensure continuous service provision. Depending on operational requirements, shifts may also include evenings, weekends, and public holidays. The nature of the role demands a flexible and responsive approach, ensuring that residents receive timely support, safeguarding interventions, and housing management assistance whenever needed.

Internal

- Customer Service Team
- Fleet and Maintenance Team

External

- Paragon system support

- Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

We work in partnership with local services to deliver accessible, high-quality support that meets people’s needs at the right time. title: GP Receptionist/Care Navigator
description: City View Medical Practice is looking for the right individual to join our reception team. You will join our dedicated team of health professionals, who have an appetite for innovation and have been part of building a successful new primary care model. You will be working within our Patient Services Area as part of our communication team, dealing directly with patients over the phone, online and at the front desk. Members of the team also carry out administrative work. An important part of your role will be care navigation where appropriate - discussing other services and treatment routes available, which may be more suitable for the patient than a GP appointment. You should be able to demonstrate excellent customer service skills and the ability to work under pressure. Good computer skills, accuracy and flexibility are essential. Experience of working in a GP surgery is not required, as full training will be provided. We are looking to recruit a full-time colleague. The shifts will vary, but are typically based between the hours of 7.30am and 6.30pm Monday to Friday. This is a flexible contract, so availability to work varying hours would be required. You will have a generous holiday allowance, enrolment in the NHS Pension Scheme and access to our Employee Assistance Programme. You will receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way, and provide general assistance to the practice team. Communicating over the phone, online and at the front desk, you will navigate patients to the most relevant treatment provider, either in practice or at another service. You will play your part in the flow of work through the practice, always adhering to practice policies and protocols. Job summary Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. Provide general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. Job responsibilities Reception Duties Navigate patients to the most relevant treatment provider. Utilise appointment system and monitor flow of patients into consulting and treatment rooms. Assist patients with understanding practice operating procedures. Advise patients of relevant charges for private services, accept payment and record in line with agreed protocol. Respond to all queries and requests for assistance from patients and visitors. Enter requests for home visits onto the computer following practice protocols. Ensure prescriptions are actioned via all channels following practice protocols. Action requests for ambulances following practice protocols. Ensure reception and waiting areas are kept neat and tidy. Adhere to correct opening and closing procedures for the practice. Management of appointment systems Book appointments according to practice protocol. Report any problems with appointment system to the Workflow Co-ordinators or the Patient Services Team Leader. Operation of telephone system Receive and make calls as required. Divert calls and take messages as appropriate, following the practice protocol. Management of medical records Register new patients following practice protocol. Ensure correspondence, reports, results etc are filed in the correct record following practice protocol. Administration/computer duties Undertake any delegated individual jobs as per practice protocols Liaise with the Workflow Co-ordinators regarding any administrative problems. Undertake any additional training required for newly delegated tasks. Any other delegated duties considered appropriate to the job.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: We are seeking a part-time receptionist to join our team working over 5 days, Monday to Friday. We are ideally wanting somebody to work 5 hours per day but the exact hours are up for negotiation at this time, and therefore we do have a degree of flexibility. This role would very much suit somebody with a caring personality and somebody who genuinely wants to make a difference. Applicants must be able to demonstrate excellent I.T skills, strong communication skills with an ability to pay attention to detail. Applicants must be able to work both independently and as part of a team. They will need to be able to adapt to the day to demands of working in a busy general practice setting. Job Summary: You will be part of a dynamic and forward-thinking team providing support in a Primary Health Care setting. You will be providing support to all patients and always demonstrating a professional disposition. Receiving calls and assisting with direct face to face patient enquiries are predominant parts of this role. To be focussed on ensuring that, the appropriate service is maintained within the healthcare environment. A professional and courteous approach at all times needs to be effective. To ensure reception; administration duties and responsibilities within the Practices are carried out accurately and in a timely fashion adhering to the guidelines and policies. The Reception Manager will be responsible for your training and day to day support. Job Responsibilities: To provide General Medical Services to patients; use of SystmOne [patient health record]; booking of appointments; dealing with queries and handling queries; requests for prescriptions; the opening and distribution of internal and external post and other office tasks. To deal with telephone calls in order to facilitate timely and appropriate communications with others and taking messages accurately and within a timely manner Professional customer service skills at all times when communicating with patients; visitors and all staff Handling specimens and ensuring the appropriate forms have been completed accurately It is essential to always have a confidential manner To establish and maintain filing and administrative systems so that written or computer information is easily accessible and secure To arrange ambulances as required Opening and closure of building Other duties may be required if requested by management staff Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members. Communicate effectively with patients and carers. Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. High standards: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the Practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk. Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision. Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance. Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs. Effectively manage own time, workload and resources. Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, Practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the Practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the Practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the Practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Are you looking for a rewarding role where you can make a real difference to people's lives every day? As the first point of contact for patients, our reception team plays a vital role in ensuring that every patient receives a positive experience when accessing healthcare. This is a varied and challenging position that would suit someone who is: Friendly, professional, and approachable Empathetic and understanding when dealing with patients Calm and resilient in a busy environment A confident problem solver Organised and able to prioritise tasks effectively Reliable, motivated, and committed to delivering excellent customer service A team player with a positive outlook Previous reception or customer service experience is desirable, and experience within a healthcare setting would be an advantage, although full training will be provided for the right candidate. In return, we offer the opportunity to work within a close-knit, supportive team where your contribution is valued and where you can make a genuine difference to the health and wellbeing of our patients. If you would like to join a practice that takes pride in caring for both its patients and staff, we would love to hear from you. Greeting patients and visitors in a professional, friendly and helpful manner. Answering telephone calls and responding to patient enquiries. Booking, amending and cancelling appointments. Signposting patients to the most appropriate service or healthcare professional. Processing prescription requests in line with practice procedures. Managing incoming and outgoing correspondence, including emails, letters and clinical documents. Registering new patients and maintaining accurate patient records. Scanning, coding and filing patient information using clinical computer systems. Liaising with GPs, nurses, hospitals and other healthcare providers. Supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. Maintaining patient confidentiality and complying with information governance requirements. Undertaking other administrative tasks as required by the practice. General Reception Duties A1. To work at the Reception Desk, greeting patients on arrival in a polite, welcoming manner. A2. To handle patient request for appointments and medication in a helpful, efficient way. A3. To answer the telephone promptly with a suitable greeting. A4. To deal with difficult, demanding patients on the phone in an appropriate manner and record telephone calls as appropriate when issues arise. A5. To ensure all messages are dealt with efficiently and appropriately making sure a contact telephone number is taken and then passed on to the relevant person(s) in an efficient and timely manner. A6. To ensure phone calls are transferred appropriately and efficiently to relevant members of staff ensuring that clinicians are free before doing so. A7. To ensuring requests from other parties (solicitors, other NHS agencies etc) are carried out within the confidentiality guidelines of the Data Protection Act (Information Governance Training will be given appropriately) and accurate records are kept of such communications as necessary. A8. To ensure online consultations requests are responded to and processed in a timely fashion A9. To advise patients of relevant charges for non-NHS and private services, accept payment and issue receipts for the same. A10. To inform the Practice Manager if a patient raises a concern or complaint with written details of the incident. A11. To complete patients request for repeat prescription items accurately and send through to the GP to sign. A12. To ensure that any items requested from the patient or patients carer that are not on the repeated items screen must requested from the Pharmacist Group detailing items requested and why they are requesting medication. A13. To deal with requests from the clinicians for patient contact or recall in an efficient timely manner. A14. To take requests from members of the public wishing to become patients issuing the appropriate information and application form and advising them of the new patient application process adopted here. A15. To ensure that all temporary patients and requests for immediate necessary treatment complete the required forms and are registered onto the system before their appointment. A16. To ensure that all New Baby registrations requests have the relevant forms completed and registered onto the system in a timely fashion. A17. To take responsibility that the signed prescription box is not accessible to the general public if ever the reception desk is left unmanned. A18. To ensure that any paper prescriptions are only collected by patients, authorised family members or pharmacies. A19. To take responsibility for all patient samples handed over the reception desk, ensuring that they have the patients details and that they are correct and are passed on to the appropriate nurse or entered into the colour coded plastic bags ready to be taken to the path labs at HRI. A20. To receive internal and external mail and deal with it appropriately, distributed to relevant trays or scanning onto the system and forwarded electronically. No items marked Private and Confidential should be opened by anyone but the intended recipient or their delegate ie, the Practice Manager will open this for the for GP when he is on leave. A21. All incoming post must be dealt with in an efficient and timely manner. A22. To input data as directed by GP, accurately and in a timely fashion onto the patients electronic record, relevant to shift worked. A23. To ensure relevant information is passed on as required for the next shift. These duties are performed by the receptionists as a team and therefore you should be able to take the initiative and perform these duties as and when required. B1. Depending on rota, to open up the surgery premises at the start of day, resetting alarm and make all necessary preparations to receive patients. B2. Depending on rota, secure the surgery premises at end of day, ensuring all fires/heaters are switched off, all doors and windows are closed & locked, surgery is totally secured, internal lights off and alarm activated. B3. To ensure external mail is posted or taken to the post office in a timely fashion. B4. To partake in the performing of processing referral letters/medical reports/supporting letters. B5. To partake in photocopying relevant to office duties (Solicitors requests from patient files, X-ray forms and any other forms required as hand outs). B6. To ensure that the appropriate details are taken and noted accurately on the visit screen when a home visit is requested. A brief summary printout and blank prescription should also be attached and placed in the visit box in a timely manner. B7. To ensure reception and waiting areas are kept neat, tidy and safe. B8. To ensure that, after use, the patient notes are accurately filed in the correct filing system, ie alphabetical order Surname, First Name. B9. To ensure all paper waste which may contain confidential information, no longer needed, relating to the surgery or a patient is put in the shredding bins as a means of disposal. B10. To take responsibility/sign for any items deliver to the practice, ensuring that they are passed onto the intended recipient or placed in the intended area, i.e. fridge immediately. B11. To receive internal and external mail and deal with it appropriately, distributed to relevant trays or scanning onto the system and forwarded electronically. No items marked Private and Confidential should be opened by anyone but the intended recipient or their delegate ie, the Practice Manager will open this for the for GP when he is on leave. B12. To act as a chaperone when requested by a clinician for an examination and ensure a record is made of your presence on the patients record. B13. Review and process incoming emails and voicemails received in the generic email inbox. Miscellaneous C1. To be prepared to offer assistance as and when necessary due to staff shortages or to an increased workload. C2. To make every effort to attend practice meetings and training arranged by the practice even if this is outside the normal hours of work. Appropriate notice will be given and time in lieu awarded. C3. To ensure an active part is taken with the general duties of maintaining running a smooth office environment. C4. To be proactive in seeking to acquire new skills which will be to the benefit of the Practice and the role employed by the practice, such as any training courses, reading etc. C5. To follow any guidance given and adhere to the Practice Protocols written by the Doctor, Nurse and Practice Manager. C6. To take responsibility at all times for the health and safety of oneself, fellow employees and patients. C7. To be aware and comply with the practices Health & Safety Policies C8. To be aware of fire procedures, how to raise the alarm, fire fighting equipment and its use, the fire evacuation procedure and your responsibilities in an emergency situation to both patients and fellow staff members. C9. To be aware of the Practice First Aid procedures and ensure the accident book is appropriately completed as necessary. C10. To be aware of the constraints of confidentiality and in particular the Data Protection Act 2018 and its relevance to you both in, and outside of work. C11. To be aware of the Good Practice Guidelines for General Practice Electronic Records and the information contained relevant to your role. C12. To be aware of the contents of the Practice IT policies and Procedures File comply with their direction regarding the use of IT within the practice. C13. To be aware of the contents of the Practice HR policies and comply with their direction. C14. To always act within the best interest of the practice, patients and employees. C15. To support the GPs, Practice Nurses, Practice Manager and all fellow employees at all times. C16. To ensure that any other (appropriate) tasks are performed as requested by the Doctor or Practice Manager taking capacity and training into consideration.
